author: Johnathan Buttweed
text_post: ER was really fucked up. But some people are just misfits in this world. They were born but they just don't belong. Kind of like a homeless guy in a really wealthy part of town.They just stick out like a sore thumb. I think to me what would be a huge difference between a "normie" and "non normie" would be that normies can find at least a decent amount of belonging. They have peers, similiar people, people they can relate to, people they can connect with, people they can belong with. They have a tribe basically. But "non normies" don't really have this. And not always necessarily because they are bad or incompetent, they are different. They don't have a group who is like them who they can belong to. And belonging to a group is huge. I don't think people really understand the huge psychological benefits you get from having similiar people to belong with and interact with. The psychological benefits are massive. If one day you stumbled upon a group who was like you and you could belong with, it'd feel pretty good. People need to part of something that both involves others and is also compatible with who they are. Deviate from that and it's not good. It's just the way your brain is designed. It's not designed in a independent manner, it's designed socially. That's also why people have social anxiety, etc. And it's why you can't just "turn it off" if you want to. It's biologically hard wired. Just like pain, etc. You can pretend and deny all you want but fact is you are a social animal, with a social brain, and that social brain is mostly in control, you are not. The only way to not be that way would be to have a totally different brain structure, one which either does not exist or is exceptionally rare and probably has other drawbacks. If you are a human being with a human brain, then you have a primarily social brain, that's just the way it is. Thus when a person does not belong, it can really cause some problems.
